thesis: Workday, Inc. sells cloud software for human capital management (HCM) and financial management to large and mid-sized enterprises worldwide. **[Fact]** FY2026 revenue (year ended January 31, 2026) was **$9.55 billion** (+13.1% versus **$8.45 billion** in FY2025), with subscription services **$8.83 billion** and professional services **$719 million**. **[Fact]** The company reports a **single operating segment** spanning Financial Management, HCM, Planning, Spend Management, and the Workday Cloud Platform. **[Fact]** Customers are chief financial officers, chief human resources officers, and IT leaders replacing legacy on-premise ERP systems. **[Fact]** Americas revenue was **$7.18 billion** (75% of total) in FY2026; EMEA **$2.38 billion**.
why_market_wrong: The market may be pricing Workday as a mature, low-margin SaaS vendor while subscription backlog and operating leverage are still compounding. **[Fact]** Remaining performance obligation (RPO) was **$28.1 billion** at FY2026 year-end, with **$8.8 billion** expected to convert within twelve months. **[Inference]** Generalists may overweight competitive fear from Oracle and SAP bundles and underweight Workday's unified data model, multi-year contracts, and AI upsell on renewals. At a premium multiple, the stock may still embed **double-digit subscription growth** that filings support but the headline price-to-cash-flow ratio obscures.
